questions.title: Exact McNemar test for paired binary outcomes
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation grounded in Quinn McNemar, Note on the Sampling Error of the Difference Between Correlated Proportions or Percentages, Psychometrika 12(2), 1947, 153-157, DOI 10.1007/BF02295996. Let (A_i,B_i), i=1,...,n, be iid paired binary observations and let N_ab count pairs with A_i=a and B_i=b. Under marginal homogeneity P(A=1)=P(B=1), derive the equivalent restriction p_01=p_10 and, by conditioning the multinomial cell counts on M=N_01+N_10, derive N_01 given M=m as Binomial(m,1/2). Define the frozen exact two-sided p-value as min{1, 2 P[Binomial(m,1/2)<=min(N_01,N_10)]}; prove conditional rejection probability is at most alpha for every m and hence unconditional size is at most alpha. Handle M=0, equal discordant counts, discreteness, and pair-order exchange. Distinguish this exact conditional test from a one-sided test, a mid-p modification, the asymptotic chi-square McNemar statistic, and a test for two independent proportions. The required model-authored artifact is est_mcnemar_exact and must implement the frozen Python run_estimator(request) contract exactly. Exploratory Python or R may diagnose identities. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment uses predeclared paired-binary null laws with equal discordant probabilities and checks exact identities plus type-I calibration with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Simulation supports implementation and calibration; it is not a proof. Source-code replication, novelty, and Lean formalization are not applicable.

source.title: Note on the Sampling Error of the Difference Between Correlated Proportions or Percentages
source.author: Quinn McNemar

request_fields.name: pairs
request_fields.meaning: The paired binary observations in stable subject order, with each row [A_i,B_i].
request_fields.shape: one nonempty outer array; every inner array has exactly two entries
request_fields.indexing: row i is one subject, first entry is A_i and second entry is B_i
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, floats, strings, values other than exact integers 0 and 1, malformed rows, nonarrays, and an empty outer array; do not coerce entries.

request_fields.name: alpha
request_fields.meaning: The predeclared significance level used only to turn the exact p-value into a rejection decision.
request_fields.shape: one finite scalar strictly between zero and one
request_fields.indexing: one value fixed for the request
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite values, zero, one, and values outside (0,1).

response_fields.name: n_pairs
response_fields.meaning: The exact number n of admitted paired observations.
response_fields.edge_cases: At least one because empty input is rejected.

response_fields.name: count_00
response_fields.meaning: The number N_00 of rows equal to [0,0].

response_fields.name: count_01
response_fields.meaning: The number N_01 of rows equal to [0,1].
response_fields.edge_cases: Zero is allowed and orientation must not be reversed.

response_fields.name: count_10
response_fields.meaning: The number N_10 of rows equal to [1,0].
response_fields.edge_cases: Zero is allowed and orientation must not be reversed.

response_fields.name: count_11
response_fields.meaning: The number N_11 of rows equal to [1,1].

response_fields.name: discordant_total
response_fields.shape: one integer between zero and n_pairs
response_fields.indexing: sum of the two off-diagonal cells
response_fields.edge_cases: May be zero, in which case the exact p-value is one.

response_fields.name: marginal_difference
response_fields.meaning: The observed B-success proportion minus the observed A-success proportion.
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals zero when the discordant counts are equal.

response_fields.name: exact_two_sided_p_value
response_fields.meaning: The frozen doubled-tail exact conditional p-value min{1,2 P[Binomial(M,1/2)<=min(N_01,N_10)]}.
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals one when discordant_total is zero or count_01 equals count_10.
response_fields.normalization: twice the smaller conditional Binomial tail, capped at one

response_fields.name: reject
response_fields.meaning: The exact decision under the public convention that the null is rejected when exact_two_sided_p_value<=alpha.
response_fields.edge_cases: False for discordant_total zero for every admitted alpha.
response_fields.normalization: exact_two_sided_p_value less than or equal to alpha

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly pairs and alpha, and the response contains exactly the nine declared response fields; missing or extra fields are rejected rather than ignored or invented.
The four cell counts are nonnegative integers summing to n_pairs, discordant_total equals count_01+count_10, and marginal_difference uses the declared B-minus-A orientation.
Permuting subject rows preserves every response field.
Swapping A and B within every pair swaps count_01 with count_10, negates marginal_difference, and preserves n_pairs, concordant counts, discordant_total, exact_two_sided_p_value, and reject.

Appending concordant [0,0] or [1,1] pairs changes only the associated concordant count, n_pairs, and the denominator-dependent marginal_difference; it preserves both discordant counts, discordant_total, exact_two_sided_p_value, and reject.
If all pairs are concordant, discordant_total is zero, marginal_difference is zero, exact_two_sided_p_value is one, and reject is false.

empirical_claims.meaning: For each frozen discordant total m and alpha, exact enumeration of N_01~Binomial(m,1/2) gives rejection probability at most alpha under the declared doubled-tail rule.

For each frozen iid paired-binary null law with equal discordant probabilities, independently generated samples have a rejection frequency compatible with the exact unconditional rejection probability and not above alpha beyond declared Monte Carlo uncertainty.
Every frozen replicate verifies the returned four cell counts, discordant total, B-minus-A marginal difference, exact doubled-tail p-value, and decision against an independent implementation.

Every confirmatory setting fixes n, alpha, and all four paired-cell probabilities before outcomes, uses probabilities summing to one with p_01=p_10, and invokes the accepted estimator through the exact public request.
